title: Active SONAR score-magnitude calibration as a 5-of-40 subset likelihood

hypothesis.null: Each target is an independent uniformly selected 5-subset of {1,...,40}, conditional on all prior draws.
hypothesis.alternative: The active SONAR scorer's pre-target score magnitudes contain information beyond rank order and induce a better calibrated distribution over complete 5-number subsets.
hypothesis.unit_of_analysis: The complete unordered 5-number target draw, not five independent Bernoulli labels.

model.score_source: Exact scores[] returned by sonarAnalogCore from src/VinciCasaLab.jsx, called only with draws.slice(0,target_index).
model.partition_function: e_5 is the fifth elementary symmetric polynomial, computed by descending dynamic programming; it exactly normalizes over all C(40,5)=658008 subsets.
model.null_control: Uniform subset distribution; equivalent to T=infinity and log-likelihood gain exactly zero.
model.tie_break: The source scorer's existing descending-score, ascending-number order; no new ranking rule.

walk_forward.validation_selection: Choose the temperature with the largest mean prequential log-likelihood gain over the uniform 5-of-40 baseline; include the uniform null as a zero-gain candidate; ties prefer the larger temperature. No blind OOS tuning.
walk_forward.target_information_rule: For target index t, scorer input is exactly archive[0:t]; target t and all later rows are excluded.

primary_endpoint.name: Prequential complete-quintet log-likelihood gain
primary_endpoint.formula: g_t(T)=log(C(40,5)) + sum_{n in D_t} log(w_{t,n}(T)) - log(e_5(w_t(T)))
primary_endpoint.interpretation: Positive cumulative gain means the sequential model assigns greater likelihood to the observed complete draws than the uniform null.

inference.primary_test: For each fixed T, exp(sum_t g_t(T)) is a likelihood-ratio test martingale under the conditional independent-uniform null because each forecast is normalized and predictable from the strict prior. Convert to a valid conservative p-value p=min(1, exp(-sum_t g_t)).
inference.family: Nine fixed finite temperatures; Holm step-down correction across their nine OOS e-process p-values.
inference.catalogue_screen: Also report Bonferroni ×43 as a conservative catalogue screen; it does not correct unknown analyst degrees of freedom.
inference.uncertainty: Circular moving-block bootstrap, block length 20, 10000 replicates, fixed seed 20261110, for descriptive 95% CI of the selected validation temperature's blind mean gain.
inference.secondary_metrics: Top-5 and Top-20 hit counts are descriptive only and are not additional confirmatory endpoints.

integrity_checks: Verify exact Git blob SHA-1 for archive, scorer, active-engine report and this protocol.
Verify every target has a strict prior cutoff and the scorer receives no target/future row.
Verify every score vector contains each integer 1..40 exactly once with finite scores.
Verify the subset partition function by dynamic programming and exhaustive small-n test; verify uniform 5-of-40 normalizer equals 658008.
Exhaustively verify subset probabilities sum to one for one representative finite-temperature forecast.
Run future-mutation invariance checks at nine fixed cutoffs.
Run deterministic replay and byte-compare report, validation, ledger, checkpoint and manifest.
limitations: The historical blind OOS cohort was already examined by earlier SONAR work, including Q100 rank calibration; it is not a virgin holdout.
The score vector is a heuristic ranking score, not a probability calibration supplied by the original engine.
This experiment evaluates the likelihood of complete 5-subsets; it does not independently prove a better winning quintet forecast.
Any positive historical result would still require a new prospective frozen cohort and the registered Q60 gate.
